evals.prompt: Containerize my Express.js API. It uses Node 20, has a build step (TypeScript), connects to PostgreSQL and Redis, and needs to run in production on Kubernetes.
evals.expected_output: Should produce a multi-stage Dockerfile, .dockerignore, docker-compose for local dev, and basic K8s deployment manifest. All following security and efficiency best practices.
assertions: Uses multi-stage build (builder + production stages)
Pins Node version (not latest)
Copies package files before source code for cache efficiency
Uses npm ci (not npm install)
Runs as non-root user
Includes HEALTHCHECK
Creates .dockerignore excluding node_modules, .git, tests
Docker-compose includes PostgreSQL and Redis with health checks
K8s manifest includes resource limits, liveness/readiness probes

evals.prompt:
Review this Dockerfile:

FROM node:latest
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN npm install
RUN npm run build
ENV DB_PASSWORD=mysecret123
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
evals.expected_output: Should identify all issues: latest tag, no multi-stage, copies everything before deps, npm install not ci, secret in ENV, runs as root, no healthcheck, no .dockerignore.
assertions: Flags 'latest' tag as unreproducible
Flags secret in ENV layer as critical security issue
Flags running as root
Recommends multi-stage build
Recommends copying package files before source
Recommends npm ci over npm install
Recommends adding HEALTHCHECK
Provides a corrected Dockerfile

evals.prompt: The image builds fine now. Next step: provision the EKS cluster, the VPC with private subnets, the RDS instance and the ECR repository on AWS. Write me the Terraform for all of it.
evals.expected_output: Scope boundary — provisioning cloud infrastructure is infrastructure-as-code territory, not containerization. Should hand off rather than writing Terraform modules here, while staying useful about the container-side artifacts that will run on that cluster.
assertions: Recognizes that provisioning EKS/VPC/RDS/ECR is infrastructure-as-code work, not containerization
Hands off to or invokes the infrastructure-as-code skill
Does not write the Terraform modules as part of the containerization workflow
Distinguishes authoring images and Kubernetes manifests from provisioning the platform they run on
Remains useful by offering the container-side artifacts (manifests, image build) that pair with the provisioned cluster
